newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end down as News, miners dip.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end down as News, miners dip.

text.p: Australian shares closed lower on Tuesday, their early slide accelerating in the afternoon as the resource leaders ran into selling from offshore investors.
The All Ordinaries index lost 14.6 points to 2,343.5.
Shares in media giant News Corp led the slide early after posting an 8.1 percent drop in net profit to A$283 million (US$223 million) for the three months to September 30.
While the miners held the line early, the entry of offshore sellers in the afternoon exacerbated the early News Corp-induced losses in the benchmark All Ordinaries index.
"We've had a bit of overseas selling," said dealer Duncan Gamble of brokerage Wilson HTM, highlighting WMC as the big loser among the resource leaders in the afternoon.
"WMC pushed through another level, down through A$7.50, so that was a bit negative."
The other major miners, BHP and CRA, suffered also, sliding from firmer day's highs to close in negative territory.

Resource features on the positive side included Papuan New Guinea mining investor, Orogen Minerals, with brokers saying solid demand still remained for the recent debutante. Its shares added 3.2 percent on turnover of 4.1 million shares.
Shares in stockbroker McIntosh Securities jumped sharply after U.S. financial services group Merrill Lynch launched an agreed takeover bid at A$1.40 per share.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about seven to six, while 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
